# Didache Chapter 9 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_009_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 9

**1** Concerning the Eucharist, give thanks in the following manner.

**2** First, over the cup:

> We give you thanks, our Father,
> for the holy vine of David your servant,
> which you have made known to us through Jesus your servant.
> To you be glory forever.

**3** Then over the broken bread:

> We give you thanks, our Father,
> for the life and knowledge
> which you have made known to us through Jesus your servant.
> To you be glory forever.

**4** As this broken bread was scattered over the mountains and, being gathered together, became one — so let your Church be gathered together from the ends of the earth into your kingdom;

**5** for yours is the glory and the power through Jesus Christ forever.

No one is to eat or drink of your Eucharist except those who have been baptized in the name of the Lord — for the Lord himself has said regarding this: "Do not give what is holy to the dogs."

---

*LOGOS notes: Ch. 9 is an extraordinary window into earliest Christian eucharistic practice, predating any of Paul's eucharistic theology in its written form (though Paul's practice surely predates the Didache). The cup-before-bread sequence (vv. 2-3) may reflect a meal structure: a cup of blessing before the meal, then bread — corresponding to the Passover order or the Kiddush cup. "Life and knowledge" (ζωή καὶ γνῶσις) suggests the dual gift of the gospel. The scattered-bread image (v.4) is the Didache's most famous passage — an ecclesiology embedded in a eucharistic prayer: the community is constituted by its gathering from dispersion, just as the grain was gathered from scattered seeds.*
